props.title: The biases that fake a great result

cards.title: Look-ahead
cards.body: Using data that didn't exist yet at that moment.

cards.title: Survivorship
cards.body: Testing only on companies that didn't go bust.

cards.title: Data snooping
cards.body: Trying 1,000 ideas and keeping the one that 'worked'.

cards.title: Cherry-picking
cards.body: Choosing the one period where your bot shines.

props.text: Overfitting: your bot memorised the past instead of learning.
props.sub: A 70% win rate on old data can flip to a loss the day it goes live.

props.title: How to spot an AI-trading scam

items.sub: No real strategy can promise profit in a volatile market. None.

items.h: It asks you to deposit into their account
items.sub: Your money must always stay in your own broker account.
Check the registration number on the SEBI site. Most are fake.

items.h: Influencers and Telegram groups push urgency
items.sub: “Act now, seats closing” is the oldest trick in the book.

props.caption: Reported losses to such scams in India ran into tens of thousands of crores in 2024.

props.kicker: THREE RULES THAT KEEP YOU SAFE
props.title: Your permanent scam shield

items.h: Money never leaves your own broker account
items.sub: Legit tools connect via API. They never hold your cash.

items.h: Verify every claim on the official SEBI site
items.sub: Type the name yourself. Never trust a forwarded link.
Risk is the price of return. Anyone hiding it is lying.

props.caption: These three habits alone stop the vast majority of investment fraud.

props.title: Why marketplace strategies look too good

items.sub: You see the strategies that happened to work — not the thousands that died.
A curve tuned to the past is designed to make you subscribe.
The moment a strategy is popular, too many people trade it and it fades.

items.h: Their incentive is subscriptions, not your profit
items.sub: They earn whether you win or lose. Remember that.

props.caption: Use marketplaces to learn the mechanics — never to blindly copy an edge.

props.title: Four emotions that break good bots

cards.title: Fear
cards.body: You kill the bot during a drawdown — right before it recovers.

cards.title: Greed
cards.body: You override its size limits after a winning streak.

cards.title: Revenge
cards.body: You force trades to win back a loss. The account bleeds faster.

cards.title: Hope
cards.body: You cancel the stop-loss, praying a loser turns around.

props.title: How a fake AI-bot pitch actually unfolds

items.h: 1 — The hook: a screenshot of huge profits
items.sub: Faked or cherry-picked. Anyone can photoshop a P&L.

items.h: 2 — The proof: a paid influencer vouches
items.sub: Borrowed trust. They're an actor, not a client.

items.h: 3 — The ask: “deposit to activate the AI”
items.sub: The instant money leaves your account, it's gone.

items.h: 4 — The trap: small fake “profits” to lure more
items.sub: You see gains on their dashboard — until you try to withdraw.

props.caption: The dashboard is a puppet show. Real profit you can't withdraw isn't profit.

props.text: If it's guaranteed, it's a lie. If it's easy, it's already gone.
props.sub: Now that you're protected, let's build real skill.
